prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Make ONE transparent 2D game obstacle for a 120x120 wu test map. FIRST image is its unique fixed footprint mask: preserve its boundary, proportions and orientation. SECOND image is the SMALL sprite used as a shared visual style and detail-scale reference. Content: flat royal monster-catching tan rope net over dusty earth, rusty low anchors and burgundy ties. The NEW footprint measures 23.40 by 19.50 world units. CRITICAL: the whole footprint is larger, but individual objects remain at the SAME WORLD SCALE as on small footprints. Intentional heavy CABLE variant: visibly multi-strand nautical cable 0.24 wu thick with twisted plies, mesh cell 2.2-2.6 wu, bell 0.45 wu tall, anchor plate 0.65 wu across, cloth tie 0.5 wu long. Larger footprints contain MORE mesh cells, using the explicitly heavier cable material; NEVER enlarge bells or ties. Bells optional, maximum four. Infer pixel sizes as feature-world-size / footprint-world-size; for example a 0.65 wu diamond is only 2.8% of this footprint's width. Cover large areas by adding more same-sized elements and terrain, never by enlarging a copied miniature. Preserve angled top-down perspective, painterly matte storybook palette, deep plum outer contour. All ground-level; human pursuers cross while player is excluded. Transparent outside mask, no exterior glow/vignette/shadow, no walls, buildings, people or text.
constraints: fixed authored orientation and footprint size; no random rotation or scale
